definitions.definition: When two different things come together and agree or match up.
definitions.example: Like two friends walking from opposite ends of a park and meeting at the same bench.

definitions.definition: A big-picture way of thinking or a model that shapes how we understand things.
definitions.example: Before people knew the Earth was round, the flat-Earth idea was the paradigm.

definitions.definition: The basic layer or foundation that everything else is built on.
definitions.example: Like the concrete floor under a carpet — the carpet is the top layer, the concrete is the substrate.

definitions.definition: Something that depends on and weakens something else to survive.
definitions.example: A tick on a dog is parasitic — it takes blood from the dog and can make it sick.

definitions.definition: To flip something upside down or reverse its meaning.
definitions.example: If you invert the word 'good' you get 'doog' — but here it means turning good into evil.

definitions.definition: Permanent software built into a device that controls how it works and can't be easily changed.
definitions.example: The software in a calculator that makes it add and subtract is firmware — you can't delete it.

definitions.definition: A system or tool that judges or measures something.
definitions.example: A teacher's grading rubric is an evaluator for student essays.

definitions.definition: To cancel or change a command or rule using more power or authority.
definitions.example: If a parent tells you to go to bed, you can't override that rule — they have more authority.

definitions.definition: The universe seen as an orderly, organized system.
definitions.example: The cosmos includes all the stars, planets, and galaxies in space.

definitions.definition: An event that seems impossible and is often thought to be caused by God or a supernatural power.
definitions.example: If someone gets better from a deadly disease with no medical reason, some call it a miracle.

definitions.definition: Individual pieces of information used to support an argument or study.
definitions.example: If you measure the height of five friends, each friend's height is one data point.

definitions.definition: A position of advantage or moral superiority in an argument.
definitions.example: In a debate, if you have better facts, you have the high ground.

definitions.definition: An argument that goes in a loop and doesn't prove anything new.
definitions.example: Saying 'I'm right because I'm right' is a circular argument.
